title: Pool of Radiance
build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

records.c: COMBAT's entry, from the linker. Points the portrait frame routine ($48C8/$48C9) at portrait_frame ($21EB) and the VIEW screen's SPELLS call ($4481/$4482) at view_spells ($1A66), puts the combat item actions in (set_actions, X = 3), doubles sprite heights and starts the game's interrupt. Each able combatant is drawn facing the other side: the party's 3D facing ($49C2) times two for side 0, turned round (+4) for side 1; event 8 runs for each. Then the timed effects age a round (age_effects) and the main window is set.

A round. Counts each side's able combatants (count_sides), then for each of the 64 entries clears its initiative and pending spell (clear_turn) and, for an able one, sets the round: its attacks with the first attack routine ($6C11, half of attacks_per_2 after event 18, the round's parity rounding odd counts up and down in turn) and with the second when it has one ($6BDA, into $6C12), its sweeps ($A5C0, from $6B98), its initiative ($A380: a d6 plus $6BEC, at least 1) and its movement in half squares ($A540: twice the movement after party_speed and event 18). Then surprise (surprise_round).

Picks who acts next: the entry with the highest initiative ($A380, 0 for one that has acted), a tie going to whichever wins a fresh random number against the leader's ($2B4C). With none left, end_of_round decides: N set ends the battle (sprites off, menu bar cleared, LIBRARY's item actions put back by restore_actions, next module POST.COM, $6E11 = 5); otherwise a new round. The chosen entry becomes the combatant in hand ($A4F4) and its record of attacks against it is cleared (start_turn). Event 7 (can_act) can make it skip; event 15 runs and its cursor shows; one whose initiative that took away skips too. Its side goes to $A4E2, and a computer-controlled one ($6C0C bit 7) plays through ai_turn ($6774), a player's through player_turn.
Moves the cursor down a row ($03CD) and prints combat message X at the text window's left edge.
Prints combat message X at the cursor's row and the window's left edge.
Prints combat message X at row A, column Y.
Prints combat message X at the cursor: its address from msg_lo ($0BF6) and msg_hi ($0C0B).
Prints the zero-terminated string at A (low) and Y (high) through print_string.
Sets the text window to the right-hand panel through set_window: the four bytes at $0970.
status_window's edges: columns 23 to 39, rows 1 to 23.
The panel (show_panel) and then the combat menu (combat_menu).

Redraws the right-hand panel for the combatant in hand: the frames (panel_frames), the window cleared, its name at row 2, HIT POINTS (yellow when below full, hp_yellow) and the hit points now, AC and the armour class from the front ($6C0F), the readied weapon's name wrapped to fit (print_weapon), and (HELPLESS), message $3C, when event 7 says it cannot act.

The combat menu MOVE VIEW AIM USE CAST TURN QUICK DONE (menu_bar, the items at $1344), event 15 first. The mask in $48F8 starts with all eight and loses TURN with no level at $6BA4 or once the combatant has turned ($A680); CAST unless a spell level has a count ($6C03-$6C0B), no spell is pending and $49E5 is 0; MOVE with fewer than two half squares of movement left; USE when bit 0 of $A440 is set or nothing is carried ($6DF9). Then the view centres on the combatant with the cursor (show_combatant).

A player-controlled turn. A combatant whose condition has bit 7 set ends its turn. A spell begun in an earlier turn ($A440 1-$7F) is cast now (cast_spell) and ends it. Otherwise the guard flag ($A480) is cleared and the panel and menu shown. Keys: Q puts the whole party on QUICK (all_quick), the space bar takes every character back from QUICK (quick_off), M switches the computer's spellcasting for QUICK characters (magic_switch); a menu item goes through menu_lo/menu_hi into the JSR at $0A96. Carry set from the item ends the turn; clear redraws the panel and menu with the cursor where it was (or on MOVE when the menu has shrunk).
The JSR the menu item's routine is patched into ($0A97/$0A98).
The menu item's routine, low byte, patched into the JSR at $0A96.
Its high byte.
The menu items' routines, low bytes: MOVE $0E08, VIEW $0AE1, AIM $0F36, USE $274F, CAST $1A6A, TURN $257A, QUICK $1437, DONE $13EE.
The menu items' routines, high bytes.
DELAY, and a spell whose casting time runs past the initiative left: initiative 1, so the combatant acts again after everyone else this round. Carry set.
GUARD: sets the combatant's guard flag ($A480 = $80), says GUARDING (message 19) and ends the turn.
Ends the turn of the combatant in hand: clear_turn for $A4F4.
Entry X has acted: initiative ($A380) and pending spell ($A440) 0. Carry set.

VIEW: sprites off, the VIEW screen (view_menu) for the combatant ($6EFC) with its readied weapon noted ($6DB6), then weapon_change, the character stored, the cursor back and the panel's frames redrawn. $2B0B tells USE that it was called from here.
Shows combat message X on the bottom row (show_message): its address from msg_lo and msg_hi.

COMBAT's 21 messages, zero-terminated: 0 HIT POINTS, 1 AC, 2 PRESS BUTTON TO TARGET, 3 EXIT, 4 MOVE/ATTACK, MOVE LEFT =, 5 GOT AWAY, 6 FAILED, 7 ABORTED, 8 WRONG CLASS, 9 YOUR TEAMMATE IS DYING, 10 SPELL:, 11 CAMP ONLY, 12 MAGIC, 13 NO EFFECT, 14 TURNING UNDEAD, 15 NOT READIED, 16 NO TARGETS, 17 'S SPELLS, 18 OFF, 19 GUARDING, 20 ON.
The messages' addresses, low bytes, by number.
The messages' addresses, high bytes: all $0B.

The end of a round: the timed effects age (age_effects) and the monsters' losses are worked out (side_losses). Every entry runs event 19, and one dying ($84) has its dying count ($A6C0) raised, dead ($83) at 10. YOUR TEAMMATE IS DYING (message 9) when a party member is (find_dying, A = $80). Returns N set to end the battle: when no party member is able ($A4FD = 0), or when no monster is ($A4FE = 0) and the player answers NO to CONTINUE BATTLE, which is asked only while $6DA0 is 0 (NO ends it at once when it is not).
The menu bar CONTINUE BATTLE : YES NO.

Rolls the damage of attack routine $A4EF: its dice ($6C13), sides ($6C15) and signed bonus ($6C17) into $A4F7, never below 0, and 0 for a routine without dice. Only a bonus of 0 or more goes on to the backstab multiplier (backstab_damage), so a backstab with a negative bonus is not multiplied. Then event 4 for the attacker and 5 for the target, with $2AFF cleared.

Takes the damage in $A4F7 (kept in $A4F8 to show) from the target ($A4F5). Less than its hit points leaves it standing. Otherwise it goes down: unconscious ($85) at exactly 0, dying ($84) below, its dying count ($A6C0) starting at the points below 0, and dead ($83) at 10 or more.
X the condition, A the points below 0: from apply_damage, and from the attack routine's direct kill ($11DB, X = $84 and A = 5).
$A4FF = 1 when the target's condition has bit 7 set: one fewer able combatant on its side ($A4FD/$A4FE), its hit points and initiative 0. Stores the entry.
Never called: prints the working character's name at the cursor's row and the window's left edge (print_name_at).

Reports an attack: the attacker's name and ATTACKS (message $29), then the target's name and AND MISSES... ($2A), or AND HITS FOR ($2B), the damage ($A4F8) and POINTS OF DAMAGE ($1A); then report_result.

After damage ($A4F8 not 0) a spell the target was casting is lost ($A440 = $80). A target that has gone down: IS KILLED ($2E) when dead, otherwise GOES DOWN ($2C), and AND IS DYING ($2D) when dying; the effects it was keeping up end (end_its_effects), event 13 runs, and one still down and not fled ($86) is drawn lying down (lie_down). Then the message pause, the window cleared and copy_parts.
MOVE/ATTACK, MOVE LEFT = (message 4) on the bottom row with the combatant's half squares of movement ($A540) halved: the squares left.
The square of the combatant in hand ($A4F4): across in X, down in A, from its entry's first two bytes (entry_address). $0DF6 for party position $6DB4, $0DF9 for entry A.
my_square for party position $6DB4.
entry A's square.
The square in the entry at ($9E): byte 0 across into X, byte 1 down into A.

MOVE: shows the moves left and keeps the starting square ($A4E3/$A4E4) and movement ($A4E6) to undo. Each step: the view centred and the cursor on the combatant; keys 1-8 or the joystick (through joystick_dir, $7AC0) give a direction; the left arrow ($5F) puts the combatant back where it began with its movement; RETURN or the button ends the move. A step off the map asks FLEE (flee_menu). A wall or obstacle (a figure in $0400) stops it. Into an empty square the enemies it leaves get their swings (free_swings), then it moves (take_step). Into an occupied square it attacks, unless its weapon has a range (byte 12): an ally there asks ATTACK ALLY first (confirm_ally). Carry set ends the turn.

Moves the combatant a square in direction $033D when its movement ($A540) covers the cost (step_cost at $7AD0: 2 straight, 3 diagonal): every square it covers moves (move_parts), its record of attacks against it is cleared (start_turn), sound 8 plays and guards it comes up to strike (guard_swings). Without enough movement, movement goes to 0. Returns A = 1, carry clear, while it can act; carry set when it has gone down or event 7 says it cannot act.

Loads party position A. An enemy returns A = 0 at once. An ally asks ATTACK ALLY: YES NO with NO lit; NO returns 1. YES sets $6E33 to $3F, which turns every NPC and monster on the party's side against it (quick_off for all 64 entries), recounts the sides and returns 0.

AIM: the targets the combatant can see within 128 squares ($0364 = $80, lines clear both ways, $0619 = 1) are listed (list_seen into $A640), NO TARGETS (message 16) when there are none. NEXT and PREV step through them, wrapping, the panel showing each with the cursor drawn along the line to it (trace_cursor); MANUAL moves a cursor freely (manual_aim); TARGET (offered when the weapon's range, $2B50, at least 1, reaches the target's distance in $9880 and the weapon can strike: $2B62 is 0) attacks it; EXIT cancels ($A4F5 and $2B54 = $FF). An attack uses up ammunition (use_ammo), turns to face, and counts a long shot ($2B42) when the target is 2 or more squares off.
No missile weapon or nothing in reach: $2B62 = 0, the weapon can strike.
Leaves AIM with no target: $A4F5 and $2B54 = $FF, $2B65 0, the file in slot 7 reloaded if needed (reload_slot7). Carry clear.

Records an attack on the target ($A4F5) from direction $033D: its count of attacks ($A3C0) goes up; the first sets its facing ($A500), and each later one adds its turn away from that facing, 0-4, to $A400.
The panel (show_panel), then centre_on.
Centres the view on party position $6DB4's square (centre_view) and draws the cursor over it (mark_square).

Turns the combatant to face the target: the two squares (both_squares), the line between them (line_between, its lengths in $0354 across and $0355 down), then one of eight directions into $033D from face_dirs: straight when one length is under half the other, otherwise diagonal; $28 and $29 say west and north.

The guards' swings at a combatant that comes up to them, for one of its squares: each guarding enemy ($A480 bit 7) that is able and can see it within 2 squares (can_see, lines clear both ways) and that event 7 lets act turns to face it and attacks, and stops guarding. Stops when the mover goes down. Puts the mover back in hand with its side; returns 0 when nobody struck, otherwise its condition plus 1 (bit 7 set when it went down).
face_target's directions, by four times the kind of line (0 diagonal, 1 mostly across, 2 mostly down) plus 2 for west plus 1 for north: SE NE SW NW, E E W W, S N S N (0 north, clockwise to 7).

The attacks on the target. Its attack routine ($A580, 1 at the start of the round) and the range modifier (range_penalty, $2B7B) are taken, the round's tallies cleared ($A4F7-$A4FC), and the target's AC figure (target_ac) set in $A4F0. A target that event 7 says cannot act is hit at once: dying ($84) with its dying count at 5, reported, and timed effect $19 on the attacker ended. Otherwise against a large target the weapon's large damage (large_damage); $2B7B is added to the AC figure, and 2 taken off it for a backstab, both of which make the roll easier. Then each attack left with routine 1 and then routine 0 ($6C11, $6C12): a roll (hit_roll); a hit rolls damage (roll_damage), applies it (apply_damage), is reported (report_attack) and runs event 2 or 3 (the routine's) for the attacker. Misses are reported only when nothing hit. A target that goes down with attacks left keeps the routine ($A580) and returns A = 1 so another can be attacked; otherwise the turn ends. finish_attacks last.
Not an entry: the frame call at $48C7 points here, at DUNGEON's draw_box_corners, until combat_start points it at portrait_frame.

One attack's roll: timed effect $19 on the attacker ends first. A d20 ($2B10): 1 always misses, 20 counts as 100 and always hits. Events 10 (attacker) and 16 (target) may change it, bit 7 making a miss. Hits when the roll, plus the to-hit figure ($6C0E, 60 less the THAC0) and the side's bonus (side_hit_bonus), reaches the AC figure in $A4F0: $A4FB = 1 and carry set.

The AC figure an attack must reach, into $A4F0 (60 less the armour class): event 11 for the target, then its figure from the front ($6C0F), or from behind ($6C10) for a backstab ($2B7C), for a swing at a combatant moving away ($2B58), and when it has been attacked at least twice since its turn ($A3C0) from directions spread 5 or more ($A400) and this attack does not come from where it faces ($A500 against $033D).
Makes entry A the combatant in hand ($A4F4) and loads it.
Loads the combatant in hand ($A4F4) through load_combatant.
A plus the round's parity: bit 0 of $2B3B, which age_effects counts up every round.
set_target, then the combatant in hand loaded again.
Makes entry A the target ($A4F5), then target_head.
When the target ($A4F5) is a secondary square of a big monster ($6C01 bit 7), the target becomes its head entry.
The frames: the whole screen's (draw_frame's corners at $4835) and the panel's (the four bytes at $1320), each through portrait_frame.
The panel's frame: columns 22 to 39, rows 0 to 23.
The attacks in two rounds: a readied weapon with flags bit 3 set (a missile weapon) gives its own count ($6D91); otherwise the character's ($6BD9) plus the round's parity (add_parity). X = $6DB4.
ANDs A into the menu mask's low byte ($48F8): takes items away.
The menu bars MOVE VIEW AIM USE CAST TURN QUICK DONE (eight items, no heading) and, at $136D, NEXT PREV MANUAL TARGET EXIT (five), as menu_bar takes them.
Moves the cursor a square at a time from the combatant to the target's square ($0348/$034A), centring the view and drawing the cursor at each step, and leaves the view centred on the target.
The menu bar ATTACK ALLY: YES NO.

DONE: the menu GUARD DELAY QUIT BANDAGE SPEED EXIT ($1456). GUARD only with a weapon of no range ($6D9D = 0), BANDAGE only while a party member is dying (find_dying). GUARD guards, DELAY delays the turn, QUIT ends it, BANDAGE binds every dying party member (find_dying with A = 0) and comes back here, SPEED sets the message speed (speed_menu) and comes back here; EXIT goes back to the combat menu.

QUICK: the combatant goes under the computer's control ($6C0C = $80) with initiative 20 (initiative_20), so it plays at once; its remembered target is dropped when that is out of the fight or on its own side (check_target). The bottom row is cleared and the key buffer emptied. Carry set ends the menu.
The menu bar GUARD DELAY QUIT BANDAGE SPEED EXIT.
The end of the bar: QUIT BANDAGE SPEED EXIT.
FB/FC = the square at $A4E3/$A4E4: where MOVE began, or MANUAL's cursor.
Never called: combat message 3 at the cursor's row, column 2 (msg_at).

When the combatant leaves its square, enemies it moves away from swing at it from behind ($2B58 = 1): each enemy that can see it within 2 squares (enemies_seen, A = 2, into $A640) that has not swung during this move ($A480 bit 0, first_swing), from which the move leads away (move_away, by the move's direction kept in $A4E5) and that event 7 lets act. It swings with an attack routine that has attacks left, or with one attack of its first routine; it turns to face first. Stops when the mover goes down ($A4FF). The mover's square, facing and side are put back; returns its condition in A.

A fighter's sweep: with fewer attacks left this round than its sweeps ($A5C0) and a target of level 0 ($6BA0, under one hit die), counts the level-0 enemies it can see within 2 squares; two or more and it sweeps them (sweep), carry clear. Otherwise carry set: an ordinary attack.
SWEEPS (message $2F), then one attack at each level-0 enemy in the list ($9800) up to its sweeps ($A5C0): it turns to face each, notes the attack and attacks with one attack ($6C11 = 1).

Surprise, in the first round only, since it clears $6DCB: when exactly one of SURPRISE's two bits is set ($6DCB = 1 or 2), side $6DCB / 2 (0 the party, 1 the monsters) loses 6 from each able combatant's initiative, down to 0.
Adds the side's to-hit bonus to A: $6E71 for side 0 (the party), $6E70 for side 1.
The movement X for the round: a monster's ($6C0C bit 0) as it is; a party member's plus $6E72, and 1 when that comes to under 2 or wraps past $C0.
can_strike for the weapon the computer chose ($2B59, an item slot), with $2B60 = 0: carry set when it can strike, and set at once when there is none.

Whether the readied weapon can strike, carry set when it can: any weapon that is not a missile weapon; a bow (flags bit 0) with arrows readied ($6DD7), a crossbow (bit 7) with quarrels ($6DD8), a thrown weapon (flags $10 and up) itself. $164A with A = 1 ($2B60) also limits this round's attacks ($6C11) to the arrows, quarrels or thrown weapons there are ($6D86) and to a thrown weapon's attacks ($6D91 / 2), and marks the item ($2B66) to be used up ($2B65).
can_strike with A in $2B60.

When the readied weapon ($6DEA) has changed since the turn began ($6DB6), the attacks this round ($6C11) are cut to the new weapon's for one round (attacks_per_2 after event 18, halved) if that is fewer. $16AF without the check.
weapon_change without the check.

After the attacks: the ammunition or thrown weapon marked ($2B65, slot $2B66) loses the attacks made ($A4F9), its slot emptied at 0; the combat figures are worked out again (compute_combat_stats), the character stored, and $2B42, $2B65, $2B7B and $2B7C cleared. Keeps A.

Fleeing. With no enemy that can see it within 128 squares it gets away; otherwise its movement (event 18) is matched against the fastest enemy's (fastest_sides): faster gets away, slower FAILED (message 6), level a coin toss. Getting away: GOT AWAY (message 5) and condition $86 on all its squares (set_condition), off the map. Ends the turn.
Sets condition A ($2B1D) on each of the combatant's squares in turn, taking each off the map (unplace_entry), then recounts the sides.
Takes party position $6DB4 off the map (remove, $C012); returns its next square ($6C02).
Puts party position $6DB4 on the map (place, $C00F); returns its next square ($6C02).
GDRIVE00's entry arguments: $9B = party position $6DB4 (or A from $1761), $B1 = 0.
entry_args for entry A.
The fastest movement on each side, after event 18: side 0's into $2B69, side 1's into $2B6A.
FLEE: YES NO; YES flees (flee), NO returns carry clear.
The menu bar FLEE: YES NO.

Against a large target (its size $2B7A, bit 7): the attacker's readied weapon's damage against large creatures ($6D8E dice, $6D8F sides) goes into the first attack routine, and its bonus changes from the weapon's small bonus ($6D97) to its large one ($6D90).
Sound 2 for a miss or 6 for a hit ($A4FB), then pause_90.
A short pause: delay with X = $5A.
Yellow text (7) when the hit points now ($6C19) are below the full hit points ($6B76), low bytes only.
Clears the record of attacks on the combatant in hand: count ($A3C0) and spread ($A400) 0, facing ($A500) none, $FF; and $2B65.
Lights the menu choice and waits for a menu key (get_menu_key), returning what it gives: the item in A, N set for none chosen.
Counts the able combatants (able_side) on each side: side 0, the party, into $A4FD; side 1 into $A4FE.
For the entry at $6C00: N set when it is empty, out of the fight (condition bit 7) or a secondary square of a big monster ($6C01 bit 7); otherwise its side (side_of) in A and X.

The enemies the combatant in hand can see within A squares ($0364): everything it sees (list_seen, $C03C, into $9800 with distances at $9880), keeping only the other side (keep_enemies). Returns how many.
Sets the line-of-sight call up from the combatant in hand: $0344 = $A4F4, $0361 = $FF, and (from $1864) groups $0346 and $0347 0.
Groups $0346 and $0347 0.

Addresses for drawing icon A ($2B3E) in pose Y ($2B3F; 0 ready and 1 action facing east, 2 and 3 the same mirrored to face west): the pose's 72 bytes at $9BE8 + 162 times the icon (+72 for an action pose) in $A3/$A4; its nine colours (+144 from the icon, +153 for an action pose) in $A9/$AA; and the nine characters it is drawn into, $D2F0 + 72 times a slot, in $A7/$A8. The slot: 17 for an action pose (16 for a big monster's second square, $2B4B), the icon's own for a party member's ready pose (icons 0-7), and 8 + 2 x (icon - 8), plus 1 facing west, for a monster's.
Copies the 72 bytes of the pose at ($A3) into the characters at ($A7), with all 64 KB RAM showing; a west-facing pose (Y 2 or 3) goes through mirror_byte.
Draws icon A in pose Y for entry X ($2B3D): icon_addresses, copy_pose, the entry's byte 2 set to icon x 4 + pose, the wide-picture shift (pose_shift), then the square drawn (draw_plain, $C04B).

Mirrors one byte of a pose left to right: a hires character (its colour, ($A9), below 8) by reversing its eight bits (mirror_bits), a multicolour one by reversing its four pixel pairs (mirror_pairs); stores it where mirror_cells says.
Reverses the eight bits of $03DE into A.
Reverses the four bit pairs of $03DE into A: multicolour pixels.
Stores the mirrored byte in the character mirror_cells gives, at the same row.
For each of a pose's nine characters (three rows of three), the offset of the one it goes to when mirrored: 2 1 0, 5 4 3, 8 7 6, times eight.

The target turns to face its attacker, unless the attack is a backstab ($2B7C) or the target is flanked (attacked twice, spread 5, as target_ac): each of its squares is drawn in its ready pose turned towards the attacker (target_poses by $033D).
The target's pose by the attacker's direction $033D: 2 (ready, facing west) for an attacker going east, 0 otherwise.
The action pose by facing $033D: 1 (east) for NE to S, 3 (west) for SW to N.
The ready pose by facing $033D: 0 (east) for NE to S, 2 (west) for SW to N.
Draws the combatant in hand in its action pose for its facing (action_poses): its first square and, for a big monster, its second ($2B4B), then back to its head entry.
Draws every square of the combatant in hand in its ready pose for its facing $033D (ready_poses), then back to its head entry.

An attack on the target: the cursor off, the backstab check (backstab_check), the target turns (turn_target), a pause, the ready and then the action pose. A missile attack ($2B42) with attacks left sends the missile's picture (missile_picture) flying to the target (fly_missile). Then the attacks (attack_routine), the ready pose, the message pause and the cursor off. Returns attack_routine's A: 1 when attacks remain after the target fell.
attack_routine, then the ready pose, the pause and the sprites off.
Not an entry: the VIEW screen's SPELLS call at $4480 points here, at CAMP's view_spells, until combat_start points it at view_spells ($1A66).
Sprite 7, the cursor, on ($D015 bit 7).
All sprites off.
The VIEW screen's SPELLS: the spell list without CAST (mask $FB).
CAST: the spell list with every item (mask $FF).

The spell list, A the menu mask ($2B7D). The memorized spells are gathered (gather_spells; an item's spells for USE, item_spells); none returns carry clear. The main window shows the name and 'S SPELLS (spell_title) and a page of the list (list_page) under SPELLS: NEXT PREV CAST EXIT, NEXT only when more follow and PREV only after the first page. CAST picks a spell from the page as a vertical menu. A spell for the camp only (bit 4 of its flags, spell_bits) says CAMP ONLY. Otherwise it becomes the pending spell ($A440); an item's (USE, $2B0C) ends the turn there for USE to cast. A memorized one leaves memory (forget_spell), the panel and the area are redrawn, and with no casting time (bits 5-6 of its flags) it is cast at once (cast_spell); with one, BEGINS CASTING ($28) and the casting time comes off the initiative, which at 0 becomes 1: the spell goes off when the caster's turn comes round again.
The window cleared, the character's name at row 2 and 'S SPELLS (message 17) after it.
Copies the combatant's entry ($6C00, kept at $9700) to each of its other squares ($6C02 on), all but bytes 1-11 and 13, which each square keeps: a big monster's squares stay alike.
enemies_seen from each of the combatant's squares in turn until one sees an enemy; then back to the head entry.
For a big monster's secondary square ($6C01 not 0), its head entry ($6C01 less bit 7) becomes the combatant in hand.
Moves each of the combatant's squares a step in direction $033D (lift_square), then back to the head entry with its square in FB/FC and the view centred.
The guards' swings (guards_strike) at each of the mover's squares in turn while it stands; then back to its head entry. Returns how many struck, in $A4EC, carry set when it went down.
Back to the head entry, A = $A4EC, carry clear.

Draws a combatant that has gone down. The target is drawn in its ready pose facing west, then sprites 2 (red) and 3 (black), pictures $88 and $89 (combat graphics set_sprites put at $E200), are placed over its square (square_on_screen), stretched for its size (body_x_size, body_y_size by the low bits of $6B99). Each of its squares keeps where it lay in its entry ($6C0A/$6C0B) and leaves the map (unplace_entry), so the others can walk there. Sprites 2 and 3 are left on.
Entry A's square as a sprite position: X = 24 x (across less the view's left column, $037E) + 32, Y = 24 x (down less its top row, $037F) + 58. Also puts the square in FB/FC.
Sprites 2 and 3 doubled across ($D01D) by the size: 0 0 0 $0C $0C.
Sprites doubled down ($D017, bit 7 the cursor) by the size: $80 $80 $8C $80 $8C.
What try_step finds on the square (who_is_at's first, $9780): N set when it is empty, or $FF when it is the stepper ($2B43) or one of its own squares; 0 for another combatant.

Moves one square of the combatant: the old tile's occupied bit (bit 7) cleared when nobody else stands there, the square stepped in direction $033D (step, $C027) and written into the entry, and the new tile's occupied bit set.
Keeps only the other side's combatants in the list of what is seen ($9800, with their distances at $9880), closing it up.
The menu bar SPELLS: NEXT PREV CAST EXIT.

MANUAL: PRESS BUTTON TO TARGET (message 2). A cursor moves freely with keys 1-8 or the joystick (joystick_dir); at each square aim_square_info shows any combatant there the aimer can see. RETURN or the button asks TARGET: YES NO, YES offered only when the square is within the weapon's range ($2B50) and the weapon can strike ($2B62 0), and there is a target other than the aimer or a square may be chosen ($2B51). YES keeps the square in $2B54/$2B55 with the target; NO cancels both ($FF).

At the manual cursor's square, kept in $A4E3/$A4E4: a combatant there that the aimer can see becomes the target and its panel shows; otherwise no target ($A4F5 = $FF), and the frames and panel are cleared.
While the computer plays: a key other than M (magic_switch), or the joystick, takes the party back from QUICK (quick_off).

Every party member back under the player's control ($6C0C = 0), from slot 7 down; $1E35 from entry A down. Empty entries and condition 3 are passed over. An NPC ($6BB8 bit 7) stays with the computer, and while $6E33 is set (the party attacked an ally) goes over to side 1 with no target ($A600 bit 7).
quick_off from entry A down to 0.
The menu bar TARGET: YES NO.
$A4E3/$A4E4 = FB/FC.
For the computer: the sweep check (sweep_check) when its range ($0364) is under 3, carry clear when it swept; carry set otherwise.
One try at a step: the heading $2B3C turned by try_turns at $2B61 (when try_gate allows), through try_step; after a step, step_done.
The turns from the heading the computer tries in a move, the last entry first: 0 straight, 1 and $FF a point either way, 2 and $FE two (ai_shuffle and morale set them).

The computer chooses its weapon from the items its class may use (weapon class 0): the best missile weapon ($2B59, score $2B5C) and the best melee weapon ($2B5A, score $2B5D) by weapon_score, and a shield (class 1, $2B5B). The missile weapon is chosen when it has one, no enemy is within 2 squares, it can strike (ai_can_strike) and half the melee score is below the missile score; otherwise the melee weapon ($2B5E = 1). The chosen weapon is readied in place of the readied one unless that is cursed, then the shield as the hands allow (ready_shield).

A weapon's worth to the computer, into $2B5F: dice times sides, plus 8 times a positive magical plus ($6D80), plus twice a positive damage bonus ($6D97). A missile weapon adds twice (its attacks in two rounds less 1); a one-handed weapon 3; a two-handed one scores 0 when the hands in use ($6DF5) leave no room, as does one whose byte 15 is $84.
Adds A to $2B5F unless it is negative.
Sets try_turns to one of the four orders at step_orders, chosen at random.
Four orders of turns, four bytes each, the first tried last: 0 -1 +1 -2, 0 +1 -1 +2, -1 +1 0 -2, +1 -1 0 +2.
Carry set to pass over a try: a turned try (not 0) other than the last while $2B63 is set. The last try ($2B61 = 0) sets $2B63.
After a step (carry clear), a straight one clears $2B63.
The shield the computer found ($2B5B): readied when the hands in use ($6DF5) are fewer than 2 and its classes include the character's, put away when more than 2.

The monsters' losses, for morale: over side 1's head entries the full hit points ($6B76) of all and the hit points now ($6C19) of the able ones, each doubled and summed. $2B68 = 100 less 5 for each twentieth of the full total still standing: the share lost, 0 to 100 in fives.

The computer's morale for the combatant in hand, carry set when it gave up. A turned undead ($A680 bit 7) flees. Otherwise when it is hurt enough (hurt_check): an NPC with the party flees; a monster flees only when its side's losses ($2B68, through event 17) are above the monsters' morale ($6DC6), and then, when it is slower than the party's fastest (fastest_sides), it SURRENDERS (message $3F, condition $85) if its intelligence ($6B15) is 5 or more. Fleeing sets $2B70 and the tries to turn from the heading (try_turns from step_orders).
For an NPC or monster ($6BB8 bit 7): carry set when its hit points now are at or below 100 less twice the low bits of $6BB8 (through event 17, morale_event) per cent of its full hit points.
$2B67 = A, then event 17 for the combatant to change it.
Party slots 7 to 0: each dying ($84) sets bit 3 of the menu mask ($48F8, BANDAGE), and with A positive ($2B71) is bandaged: condition $85, unconscious and no longer dying.

For a picture two squares wide (its entry's byte 3, bits 1-2): turning between the east poses (0, 1) and the west ones (2, 3) moves the square it is drawn from one across (byte 0) and flips bit 0 of byte 3; another combatant on the new square is hidden (hide_others). Byte 3's bit 7, the hidden flag, is cleared first.
A record standing for several monsters ($6BFB 2 or more) uses up its arrows or thrown weapon ($2B65) only one time in $6BFB + 1.
When the computer is fleeing ($2B70), the enemies it leaves get their swings (free_swings).

Draws a box (draw_box, A and X its four edges) and its corners: frame_corners' characters in colour 10, then the text colour back (text_colour_back). LIBRARY calls it through $48C8 to frame the portrait.
The corners in text colour A. Nothing in COMBAT calls it; the VIEW screen's DROP call at $447A points here, at CAMP's drop_money, which COMBAT leaves.
The corner characters: top left $25, top right $24, bottom left $1B, bottom right $00.

A round passes for the timed effects: each ($4900) whose time ($4980) is in minutes (top bits 0) and not 0 loses one, and one reaching 0 ends (end_effect) with its holder in hand. The round count ($2B3B) goes up and the game clock a minute (from $49C7, each figure carried at its limit).
Not an entry: the VIEW screen's TRADE call at $4470 still points here, at CAMP's trade_money; COMBAT leaves it.
The RTS that age_effects ends with; clock_limits are read from one after it.
The game clock's limits from the minutes: 10 minutes, 6 tens, 24 hours, 30 days, 12 months, then the year's $FF.
sound_start ($BA03): sound A.

SPEED: GAMESPEED (n) : SLOWER FASTER EXIT, n the message speed ($49FC, written into the bar at $22BA). SLOWER adds 1 and FASTER takes 1 off (speed_steps), within 0 to 9; EXIT, or nothing chosen, returns.
The change for SLOWER (+1) and FASTER (-1).
The menu bar GAMESPEED (0) : SLOWER FASTER EXIT; the 0 at $22BA is the speed.
The speed's digit in GAMESPEED (0), written by speed_menu.
Q: every entry under the computer's control ($6C0C bit 7) with no target remembered ($A600 bit 7).
Hides the first combatant on square FB/FC other than entry $2B3D: bit 7 of its entry's byte 3.

The computer chooses a spell, carry set when it casts: always for an NPC or monster, for a QUICK party member only with MAGIC on ($2B7F), and only while the other side has someone able. A d7 passes ($2B04), the bar ($2B12) starting at 7 and lowered each pass; in each, three random picks from the memorized spells: a spell whose priority (low bits of its byte at $DC9F, spell_info) reaches the bar and whose level has a count left is cast when bit 3 of that byte is set, or when an enemy is within its range (load_spell_record, caster_level, spell_range); it is cast through spell_menu's choice ($1B14) with $2B20 bit 7 set.

Takes spell A out of memory place Y ($2B11): one off its level's count ($6C02 + the level), and the place cleared, except that when $6BFB (the number of monsters the record stands for) is 1 or more it stays unless a random 0 to $6BFB comes up 0. Then the character is stored.
Event 7 for entry A: returns $A4FC, 0 when it can act, with the working character loaded again.
Marks the item in hand readied ($6D82 bit 7), stores it and puts its effect on (item_effect).
Clears the readied bit of the item in hand, stores it and takes its effect off.
M: MAGIC (message 12) on the bottom row, $2B7F turned over, and OFF (18) or ON (20); then the message pause. $2B7F lets QUICK party members cast (ai_cast).
Forgets the combatant's remembered target ($A600 = $FF) when that is out of the fight or on its own side.

The computer uses a magic item, carry set when it does: not when bit 0 of $A440 is set or the other side has nobody able. A d7 passes as in ai_cast; in each, the items 15 to 0: one readied, not of classes $0B-$0D, without an effect of its own (byte 15 bit 7) and with a spell (byte 14, $6D8A; above $38 less $17) whose priority reaches the bar is used (use_item) with $2B20 bit 7 set.
The bar for the computer's spells and items ($2B12 = 7) and the number of passes ($2B04, a d7).
A = $A440 for the combatant in hand, X its entry.
The other side's able count ($A4FD or $A4FE).
The entry's side, $6C0C bit 0, in A (0 the party's, 1 the monsters'); Z set when it is the side in hand ($A4E2).
The combatant in hand becomes the target ($A4F5) and its side is kept in $A4EB.
Moves on to the combatant's next square ($6C02), which becomes the one in hand: A = $FF. A = 0 when there is none.
Entry A's square into $0348 (across) and $034A (down), where a line begins.
The square of the combatant in hand into FB/FC.

Turning undead. A d20 ($2B74) is rolled once, then up to a d12 ($2B79) undead are tried, nearest first (nearest_undead), stopping at the first the roll does not beat (turn_roll). Each one beaten is shown: destroyed ($2B77 not 0), it is drawn down (lie_down), message $12 shows (IS CURSED in SPELLN00) and its condition becomes $82; turned, it is marked ($A680 bit 7) and IS TURNED (message 9). $2B78 counts down from 6 as they are affected; when the d12 runs out after a destroyed one with more to come ($2B77 = $FF) and fewer than six were affected, one more is tried. NO EFFECT (message 13) when none was.

Whether the turning roll ($2B74) beats undead type $2B75, carry set when it does, by COMBAT3's tables at $7AD7, $7AE4 and $7AF1 and the turning level ($6BA4). Below the level at $7AE4 only a 20 works, and only from the level at $7AD7; from it the number needed is $7AF1's less 3 for each level above. A number of 0 down to -4 (each 1 higher for types 0 and 1) turns it whatever the roll, destroys it from -5 to -12 ($2B77 = 1), and below -12 destroys it with more to come ($2B77 = $FF).
TURN: TURNING UNDEAD (message 14), the combatant marked as having turned ($A680), turn_undead, the sides recounted; ends the turn.
The computer turns undead for a combatant that has not yet ($A680), has a turning level ($6BA4) and sees an undead (nearest_undead): carry set when it did.
The spell list: the first spell on the page shown.
The first spell of the next page.
The spell being listed.
How many spells were gathered into $9700.
The level of the last spell listed, for the headings.
The new level when a heading is due.
Collects the memorized spells (the 81 places at $6B20, last first) into $9700, how many into $25AA.

Lists a page of spells from $25A7 as a vertical menu in the window from row 3: before the first spell of each level its heading (1ST LEVEL, 2ND LEVEL, 3RD LEVEL or 7TH LEVEL), then each spell's name (print_spell_name) two columns in, the item's key its number; then the menu is kept at $9780 (save_menu).
Works out how many spells from A fit on a page, allowing two more rows for each level heading, up to row 21: $25A8 the first that does not.
Spell $9700 + X's level (spell_level): Z set when it is the same as the last one's ($25AB), otherwise A the new level, kept.
Row 3 and no level yet ($25AB = 0).
The RTS page_reset ends with; the headings' low bytes are read from one after it, by level.
The level headings' addresses, low bytes, for levels 1 to 4 (spell_level's numbering); the high bytes follow at $2686. The fourth is RESTORATION's 7TH LEVEL.
The fourth heading's low byte ($A8), then from $2686 the high bytes ($26), read from here by level.
The headings 1ST LEVEL, 2ND LEVEL, 3RD LEVEL and 7TH LEVEL.
NEXT: the page starting at $25A8.
PREV: steps the page's start back until a page from there would end where this one began.
Copies the menu's items (count $6E93, the tables $6E96-$6EE5) to $9780-$97D0, where the redraws leave them.
Copies them back, as a vertical menu.
Spell Y's level: 1 for spells up to $15, 2 up to $23, 3 up to $37, and 4 for $38, RESTORATION.

The spells of the item in hand (bytes 13-15, $6D89-$6D8B, those not 0) into $9700, how many into $25AA: for a scroll (class $0C) in the hands of a character with a magic-user level ($6BCA), or for any item whose name is fully known ($6D82 bits 0-2 clear); otherwise none.
Entry $9800 + X (the list of what is seen) becomes the target and is loaded, when there is one.
Never called: X = 0 and on into target_from_list.
Entry $A640 + X (the list of targets) becomes the target and is loaded, when there is one.
set_target, then load_target.
Loads the target ($A4F5) when there is one; A = $A4F5.

USE: sprites off, the main window cleared, the readied weapon noted ($6DB6), the item actions' cursor on the first, the magic shown (check_detect), the frame and the items screen (item_menu), whose USE runs use_item. When an item was used ($2B0A) the turn ends; otherwise weapon_change and back to the menu.

The item action USE, for players and the computer. An item that is not readied: NOT READIED (message 15). A scroll or the like (classes $0B to $0D) lists its spells (item_spells, spell_menu with $2B0C = $FF); the one chosen is cleared from the item, its byte 2 ($6D7E) loses one and the item goes when that reaches $D1, and it is announced (announce_spell). Another item casts its spell (byte 14, $6D8A; above $38 less $17), none for an item with an effect of its own (byte 15 bit 7), CAMP ONLY for a camp spell; it uses a charge (byte 13, $6D89), one of a stack ($6D86) going when the charges run out and the item when nothing is left, and says USES AN ITEM ($23). The spell is cast at caster level 6 ($2B05) through load_and_cast, and $2B0A = 1. A player's USE then leaves the items screen (and the VIEW screen, $2B0B) by dropping their return addresses.
With Z set the item in hand is gone ($6D7C = 0); then it is stored (store_item_char).
Finds the readied items (find_readied) and loads the readied weapon ($6DEA) with its type (load_item_full): A its slot, N set when there is none.
LIBRARY's item actions back: READY $4630, USE none, TRADE $4743, DROP $47DA (set_actions with X = 7).
Copies four item actions, READY, USE, TRADE and DROP, into item_actions from action_lo/action_hi + X - 3: with X = 3 the combat ones, READY $286F, USE $277D, no TRADE, DROP $288A.
The item actions COMBAT sets, low bytes: combat's READY, USE, TRADE and DROP at 0-3, LIBRARY's at 4-7.
The high bytes.
Combat's READY: LIBRARY's (ready_item), then the item's effect put on or taken off (item_effect).

When the item in hand carries a timed effect (byte 15, $6D8B, bit 7 set: the kind), runs that effect's routine (run_effect) with A = 0 when the item is readied and $80 when it is not: the effect put on or taken off.
Combat's DROP: LIBRARY's (drop_item); a dropped item ($6D7C now 0) has its effect taken off (item_effect), otherwise the combatant is loaded again.
Combat message X on the bottom row: the bar cleared, the menu window, the cursor home, then the message (msg_left).
Carry set when the combatant ($6DB4) has a timed effect or item of kind $6E6E (has_item_type).
Target $A640 + X (target_from_list), then pick_target.
When the target is not the combatant itself, event 1 runs for it; A = the target ($2B17), N set for none.
Waits by the message speed ($49FC); none at 0.
Makes entry A the party position in hand ($6DB4) and, unless it is already loaded ($6DAA), loads it and its character (load_member's $4415). X = its condition.
Ends timed effect $19 on the combatant in hand when it has one (find_entry, end_effect).
Party position $6DB4 loses its turn: initiative and pending spell 0 (clear_turn), and its guard flag ($A480) and movement ($A540) 0.
store_item, then the member and its character stored ($441E).
The text colour back to the windows' ($6E34).

For the spell files: the combatants within X squares of the point $2B54/$2B55 that a line from it reaches, all directions ($0361 = $FF), into the target list ($A640, count $2B13). $2903 takes the directions in A.
spell_targets_at with the directions in A.
What can be seen from the point at $0348/$034A rather than from a combatant ($0344 = $FF): range X ($0364), directions A ($0361), through list_seen.
The point $2B54/$2B55 into $0348/$034A.

After a spell's effect is added (spell_effect): a target that event 7 now says cannot act loses its turn (lose_turn); then the effect's message ($2B38, none when negative) with the sparkle (report_sparkle).
The name and message X (name_message), then the sparkle over party position $6DB4 for twice the message speed plus one: pictures 3, 4 and 5 (sparkle with X = 3).

Sprite 6 over party position $6DB4's square, cycling three pictures from X ($2B1F) through missile_pictures, A + 1 times ($2B1B), with a pause of 100 between; nothing for one out of the fight. Sprites off and the window cleared after.
In the panel from row 10: the window cleared, the working character's name, then SPELLN00 message X below it (spell_message).
The next row at the left edge, then SPELLN00 message X (string X + $39).
Prints SPELLN00's string X: its address from $AF00 (low) and $AF80 (high); the spell names are 1-$38 and the messages from $39.
Never called: X = $2B38 and on into report_msg.
name_message, the message pause, the window cleared.
name_message in a window from the row after the cursor's.
When a combatant goes down the timed effects it holds end: every kind from $7F down to 1 that is not among keep_kinds is looked for on party position $6DB4 (find_entry) and ended (end_effect).
The twenty kinds of timed effect that stay on a combatant that goes down.

For the spell files: applies the spell to each target in the list ($A640, $2B13 of them; with none it returns to the spell file's own caller): a saving throw (save_roll), damage (spell_damage) and the timed effect (spell_effect). The effect's fourth byte ($2B09) is the caster's level ($2B05 low bits) unless set. $29FC keeps the damage set in $2B00.
spell_area keeping $2B00.

For the spell files: condition A ($2B1D) for party position $6DB4, which goes back on the map, each square where it lay ($6C0A/$6C0B); when one of them is taken it is killed instead ($83 on all its squares). Then copy_parts, the panel, and GETS BACK UP (message $16).
Keeps $0348-$034B, a line's ends, at $2B2E.
Puts them back.
For the spell files: adds timed effect X with time A to the target (spell_effect's $9A0D), without a message ($2B38 bit 7). The fourth byte ($2B09) is $FF; $2A97 takes it in Y.
add_effect with its fourth byte in Y.
The characters that may end a line of the weapon's name: space, comma, plus and minus.

Prints the readied weapon's name at the cursor. When it runs past the panel (the screen at $CD7F, row 8 column 39, holds none of name_ends) its last word moves down: the characters after the last space in columns 23-38 of row 8 and those print_string put on row 9 go to $A4C0, are blanked, and are printed again from the left edge.
Moves a screen character from $CD57 + Y to $A4C0 + X and blanks it.
The timed effect's time (spell_effect, add_effect).
Not used: the byte after eff_time.
The timed effect's kind.
The saving throw (save_roll): the roll as adjusted; bit 7 set when the target failed or had none.
The kind of a spell's damage, for its report: bit 0 fire, 1 cold, 2 electricity, 3 magic, 4 acid (FROM FIRE ... FROM ACID); roll_damage clears it.
The damage the spell file set, 0 for none.
Not used: the byte after spell_dmg.
run_effect's entry being checked for an area effect, 63 down to 0.
Not used: the byte after area_entry.
The computer's passes over its spells or items (a d7).
The caster's level for the spell (6 for an item's).
spell_area's place in the target list.
spell_area's number of targets.
The saving throw needed (save_roll); the speed menu's last choice.
The timed effect's fourth byte ($4B80): the caster's level, $FF from add_effect, $7F for some spells; one with bit 7 set has its routine called again when it ends.
USE: 1 once an item has been used, which ends the turn.
1 while USE is reached from the VIEW screen.
$FF while the spell list shows an item's spells (USE).
1 while event 18 works out movement (event18_move) rather than attacks.
Not used: the two bytes after move_event.
The attack's d20 roll, 100 for a 20.
The spell's place in memory (forget_spell); the computer's random pick from the target list.
The lowest priority the computer accepts this pass, from 7 down.
How many targets are in the list at $A640.
into_targets' place.
The file slot 7 is to hold again, bit 7 set when it must be reloaded (reload_slot7).
A loop count: entries, picks, spells.
The target, kept round event 1.
Not used: the byte after kept_target.
The value event 18 works on: attacks or movement.
fly_missile: 0 a plain picture; otherwise sprite 6's colour cycles, and the picture too when positive (next_missile_picture).
The sparkle's repeats.
The sparkle's and the missile's picture count.
The condition set_condition and get_back_up set; the missile picture shown.
The missile picture's colour pair (missile_pictures, from $DCE1).
The sparkle's first picture.
Bit 7 set when the computer (or a magic item) chose this turn's spell or item; pick_next clears it.
run_effects' place in the event's list.
run_effects' entry.
The A an effect's routine is called with (run_effect).
spell_range's working byte.
save_line's four bytes.

The spell's nine-byte record (load_spell_record, from $D81B): $2B32 its range ($FF for a spell that needs a hit roll), $2B33 the time's base (low six bits), $2B34 the time per level, $2B36 its saving throw, $2B37 the timed effect's kind, $2B38 the effect's message, $2B39/$2B3A the spell's routine.
The time's base, low six bits.
The time per caster level.
The saving throw: 0 none; bits 0-1 1 for no damage on a save (half otherwise); bits 2-4 which of the five saves ($6B9A); bits 5-7 an adjustment.
The timed effect's kind, 0 for none.
The effect's message, SPELLN00 message number; negative for none.
The spell's routine, low byte ($2B3A high): load_and_cast jumps to it.
The spell's routine, high byte.
Counts up each round (age_effects); bit 0 is the round's parity.
The computer's heading: towards its target, or away when fleeing.
draw_pose's entry.
draw_pose's icon.
draw_pose's pose, 0-3.
A count: end_its_effects' kind.
The spell chosen.
1 for a missile attack, a shot at 2 or more squares: range_penalty and the missile picture use it.
The combatant try_step moves.
name_message's message.
fly_missile: the first square of the line in view (across, down at $2B46), then its screen position.
The first square in view, down.
The last square of the line in view (across, down at $2B48), then its screen position.
The last square in view, down.
fly_missile's loop count.
1 when the line runs out of the view and the view must move for another leg.
1 while action_pose draws a big monster's second square (slot 16).
pick_next's random number for the leader, for ties.
Not used: the byte after tie_break.
keep_enemies' count kept.
keep_enemies' place.
AIM: the weapon's range ($6D9C), at least 1.
Not 0 when a square may be chosen rather than a combatant (a spell file's aiming); AIM clears it.
1 when AIM attacks; 0 when a spell file uses the aiming and takes the target back.
AIM's menu item.
The square chosen ($FF none): MANUAL's, and the point for spell_targets_at; down at $2B55.
The square chosen, down.
The level-0 enemies counted, then the place in the list.
The sweeps left.
1 during free_swings: the swings use the rear AC.
The computer's weapon: the best missile weapon's slot, then the one chosen.
The best melee weapon's slot.
The shield's slot.
The best missile weapon's score.
The best melee weapon's score.
1 when the melee weapon was chosen.
The weapon's score (weapon_score).
1 when can_strike limits the attacks and marks the ammunition.
The try in hand, 3 down to 0 (try_turns).
AIM: 1 when the weapon cannot strike: a missile weapon without ammunition or with an enemy within 2 squares.
Set when the last try was needed (try_gate).
Not used: the byte after straight_only.
1 when the attacks use up the item at $2B66 (arrows, quarrels or a thrown weapon).
The item to use up.
The morale figure events 17 work on.
The monsters' share of hit points lost, 0 to 100 (side_losses).
The fastest movement on side 0; side 1's at $2B6A.
The fastest movement on side 1.
side_losses' hit points now, 16 bits.
side_losses' hit points now, high byte.
side_losses' full hit points, 16 bits.
side_losses' full hit points, high byte.
Not used: the byte after full_sum.
1 while the computer's combatant is fleeing.
find_dying's A: positive to bandage.
free_swings' keeping of the mover's square (across, down at $2B73).
free_swings' keeping of the mover's square, down.
The turning roll.
The undead type (nearest_undead), then its distance.
The undead found.
turn_roll: 0 turned, 1 destroyed, $FF destroyed with more to come.
The undead affected, counted down from 6.
The undead still to try (a d12).
The target's size ($6B99): bit 7 large.
The range modifier (range_penalty): 0, -2 or -5.
The backstab multiplier, 0 for none (backstab_check).
spell_menu's menu mask.
AIM: 1 when PREV steps back through the list.
MAGIC ON: QUICK party members cast spells.
